reranked_evidence.title: 'I am still alive': Indian activist on hunger strike for 26 days loses 11kg - BBC
reranked_evidence.snippet: Indian activist and educationist Sonam Wangchuk, who has been on a hunger strike for 26 days in support of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), says he has lost 11kg (24lb) but is "still alive". Popularly known as "Sonam sir", Wangchuk has been the main draw at the youth-led movement seeking education reforms and the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. He was forcibly removed from the CJP's protest venue at Delhi's Jantar Mantar on Saturday and taken to hospital from where he continues his fast. Meanwhile, thousands continue to turn up at the protest venue even after the brutal police crackdown on Monday's march to parliament which left dozens of protesters and policemen injured. Modi has not commented directly on the protests or engaged with the protesters, but on Thursday, he posted a statement on X that is being seen as an attempt to reach out to students who have been frustrated with repeated exam paper leaks.

reranked_evidence.title: India ‘cockroach’ activist Sonam Wangchuk ends hunger strike as protests spread - The Guardian
reranked_evidence.snippet: # India ‘cockroach’ activist Sonam Wangchuk ends hunger strike as protests spread. Sonam Wangchuk halted strike amid concerns about ‘possible violence’ in India as protest movement urges demonstrations across country on Friday over police brutality. Indian “cockroach” activist Sonam Wangchuk ended a 26-day hunger strike on Friday over an exam paper scandal that has spiralled into a wideranging youth-led protest against Narendra Modi’s government, with protesters continuing to call for the education minister to resign. Wangchuk said on social media that he ended the hunger strike in Delhi in the presence of two federal ministers at the urging of scores of members ⁠of parliament, and after “a long negotiation on various conditions and in view of possible violence in the country”. Protests under the Cockroach Janta party (CJP) ​movement have called for nationwide demonstrations on Friday ‌in solidarity with students who alleged police brutality during a march on parliament on Monday by tens of thousands of people, even as Modi’s government urged them to join talks.

reranked_evidence.title: CJP's parliament march from Jantar Mantar: India's 'cockroach' protest continues a day after police crackdown - BBC
reranked_evidence.snippet: # India's 'cockroach' protest continues a day after police crackdown. Thousands have gathered again in the Indian capital Delhi a day after a police crackdown on supporters of India's Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a youth-led movement seeking education reforms and resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. Tens of thousands of young men and women had turned up for Monday's protest and tried to march on parliament, defying a police ban. Police said 118 of their personnel were also injured and 70 protesters have been detained. Police and Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government have not commented on the use of sticks and tear gas against protesters. The meeting took place against the backdrop of tens of thousands of people turning up from all over the country to participate in the CJP's call to march to parliament on the opening day of the monsoon session.

reranked_evidence.title: Indian police forcibly hospitalize a prominent Cockroach Party activist on hunger strike - NBC News
reranked_evidence.snippet: # Indian police forcibly hospitalize a prominent Cockroach Party activist on hunger strike. Police said activist Sonam Wangchuk was taken to hospital after his health worsened during the hunger strike, and that a brief commotion occurred when some protesters tried to block the move. NEW DELHI — Police forcibly transferred a prominent activist to a hospital in New Delhi on Saturday after his health deteriorated during a 20-day hunger strike tied to India’s viral Cockroach Janta Party movement for education reform. Authorities tightened security around New Delhi’s Jantar Mantar, a designated public protest ground enclosed by police barricades, where activist Sonam Wangchuk has been camped along with students and Cockroach Party activists who demand the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, after allegations that exam papers were leaked in advance. Delhi Police said Wangchuk was taken to hospital after his health worsened during the hunger strike, and that a brief commotion occurred when some protesters tried to block the move.

NEW DELHI — Police forcibly transferred a prominent activist to a hospital in New Delhi on Saturday after his health deteriorated during a 20-day hunger strike tied to India’s Cockroach Janata Party movement for education reform. Delhi police said that Wangchuk was taken to the hospital after his health worsened during the hunger strike and that a brief commotion occurred when some protesters tried to block the move. The Cockroach Janata Party — a play on the name of India’s ruling Bharatiya Janata Party — said in a social media post that the government “forcefully abducted” Wangchuk “without his or his family’s consent” two days before their planned march to India’s Parliament.
